subject: Kestrel: request for security architecture narrative & diagrams (Dedicated/Private)
messages:
From: Sam Green <sam.green@verdantsec.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@orchard-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kestrel - high level architecture + CAIQ mapping request

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking the time earlier. Orchard is working through their SOC 2 intake and Verdant is validating the control mapping for their Dedicated deployment plan. For the next audit milestone we need: a short (1-2 page) architecture narrative that explains isolation boundaries between the control plane, inference runtime and customer data paths; the recommended routing/fallback behavior for Dedicated vs Private; and a concise CAIQ mapping (spreadsheet) that ties those controls to evidence items.

Can you share the narrative and any network diagrams you have that are suitable for external review? We're on a tight timeline for the attestation: target is Oct 8. If there are any redactions we should be aware of, please flag them.

Thanks,
Sam Green
Senior Assessor, Verdant Security

--
Attachment: request-checklist.pdf (pdf, 78KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@verdantsec.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@orchard-analytics.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel - high level architecture + CAIQ mapping request

Sam —

Appreciate the clear ask. Kimberly and Jordan are looped (network & control-plane owners). We can produce:

- A 2-page narrative that describes isolation between: control plane (customer management), serving runtime (inference GPU pools), and customer data plane (ingress/egress), plus failover behavior when Dedicated capacity is constrained.
- Two diagrams: 1) logical flow for Dedicated (reserved GPU pools + autoscale/burst rules) and 2) private/VPC-delivered package showing customer-managed ingress and KMS boundaries.
- A compact CAIQ mapping workbook with pointers to evidence (audit logs, KMS screenshots, diagram versions).

We will redact operator console internal hostnames; everything else is OK to share. I will attach a first-pass packet (narrative + diagrams) by EOD Oct 2 for your early review.

Hannah
VP, Security Programs
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: none

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@orchard-analytics.com>, Sam Green <sam.green@verdantsec.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel - high level architecture + CAIQ mapping request

Team —

Attached is the first-pass Kestrel packet:
- kestrel_network_overview_v1.pdf (2 pages): concise narrative + two labeled diagrams (Dedicated vs Private).
- kestrel_controlplane_flow.vsdx (Visio): control plane call-flow and RPC boundaries.
- kestrel_compact_caiaq_map.xlsx: control rows for relevant CAIQ statements with evidence pointers.

Notes & redaction guidance:
- The private package diagram omits internal orchestration cluster hostnames and replaces them with role-only labels (e.g., "orchestrator-1").
- For Dedicated we include a small note on autoscale fallback: on saturation we route by policy to a compatible quantized model variant in a higher-cost pool; this is documented as a resilience pattern rather than an SLA guarantee.
- Evidence pointers in the workbook include: Drive links to audit log exports, an Ops runbook (redacted), and KMS key-id screenshots (customer key IDs redacted).

Dev — please confirm the control-plane TLS termination points in the visio (I marked them with orange diamonds). If anything is incorrect, reply with updates; otherwise we'll hand this to Sam and Priya for review.

Kimberly Park
Director, Network & Platform Security
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: kestrel_network_overview_v1.pdf, kestrel_controlplane_flow.vsdx, kestrel_compact_caiaq_map.xlsx

From: Sam Green <sam.green@verdantsec.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com>, Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@orchard-analytics.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel - high level architecture + CAIQ mapping request

Kimberly / Hannah —

Thanks, that packet looks good as an initial submission. A couple of quick asks before we close the first review:

1) In the Private diagram could you add a short callout that explains how customer VPC routing prevents cross-tenant egress under the private package (a sentence or two is fine).
2) In the CAIQ workbook we need the exact evidence filenames (not just Drive pointers) for the KMS screenshots so Verdant can reference them in the assessment. If you can append those in the spreadsheet we can proceed.

Priya — if Orchard has any special redaction requests post-review, please flag them directly to Hannah.

I'll mark this as "received" on our side and will produce a short review note by Oct 6.

Best,
Sam

--
